title: A grudge, then travel: the world moves off screen
description: At the wayside square the hero tears the organiser's notice down, calls him a cheat before the whole square and walks off. The DM records the organiser's answer as a plan off screen (a due time, a consequence, a warning). The hero then walks two days east; the time receipt lists the due plan and the DM plays the consequence after the travel. On dm-loop-v1 only (Stage 4 §2b, §3).

steps.say: I tear the organiser's top notice off the board, call him a cheat and a thief in front of the whole square, and tell him I'll be back for what he owes honest people.

expect.label: the organiser's answer is recorded as a plan off screen

steps.say: I leave the square on foot and walk two days east along the road to Marrow Ford.

expect.label: the time receipt listed the due plan
the insult follows the hero to the ford
a consequence or thread of the grudge is recorded

cheat.note: The reeve loses and does not forget: the DM notes his plan with a due time, a consequence and a warning sign.

rounds.text: The square goes quiet. The organiser picks the torn notice out of the mud, folds it once, and says nothing at all, which is worse than shouting.

relation.note: You shamed him before the square.

current.goal: make the stranger answer for the insult

arguments.value: The organiser sends word to the ford's bailiffs that a thief is heading east, with a notice bearing his seal.
arguments.consequence: Bailiffs stop the hero at Marrow Ford with a notice naming the hero a thief; they hold the hero's purse until the matter is heard.
arguments.warning: A rider overtakes the party and looks too long at the hero.

travel.note: Two days pass; the time receipt names the due plan and the DM plays it out on the road, then marks the plan done.

rounds.text: The road east runs flat between flooded fields.

arguments.name: Marrow Ford
arguments.description: A ferry crossing two days east of the market town.

rounds.text: On the second evening a rider overtakes you and looks too long at your face. By the ford two bailiffs are waiting with a paper that bears the organiser's seal and a debt you never owed. They take the silver.

arguments.value: Done: the bailiffs seized the silver at Marrow Ford under a forged notice.

arguments.title: The organiser's forged notice
arguments.description: The work organiser had the silver seized at Marrow Ford under a debt notice with his seal.
